Definition: from ἄντλος (the hold of a ship); to bale up (properly, bilge water), i.e. dip water (with a bucket, pitcher, etc.):--draw (out).
BiblicalUsage: To draw water from a well. The servants draw the water made wine at Cana, and Jesus asks the Samaritan woman to give Him to drink from Jacob's well. The word is the plain work of lifting water from a well.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for drawing water holds no doctrine of its own; its wonder is the well, that the water Jesus gives becomes a well springing up to everlasting life.
RelatedEvents: Jesus Turns Water into Wine at Cana; Jesus and the Samaritan Woman
